## Your part in each phase

| Phase | What is yours |
|---|---|
| [Phase 1. Engagement and scoping](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd) | State the decision the analysis supports and the deadline, and agree the assurance level with the analyst |
| [Phase 2. Design](../02-design/index.qmd) | Approve the design before the work proceeds |
| [Phase 3. Analysis](../03-analysis/index.qmd) | Stay available for the questions the work turns up |
| [Phase 4. Delivery and sign-off](../04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.qmd) | Confirm the analysis meets the need you commissioned it for |
| [Phase 5. Review](../05-review/index.qmd) | Ask whether it informed the decision, and whether it is still being used |

## Three things only you can do

- **State the decision, not the output.** What will be decided, by whom, and by when. That makes
  the conversation about scope a short one.
- **Agree the level, and find what it needs.** The level is scored with the analyst at scoping, in
  about five minutes, and it then costs time and somebody's diary. Where that cost cannot be met,
  the answer is a narrower question rather than a lower level.
- **Own the use of the results.** Caveats travel with the number. A result passed on without them
  has had its limits removed by the act of passing it on, and how the analysis is used and
  disseminated is yours.

## Where your approval is needed

The design, before the work proceeds, and the results at sign-off where the level says the
sign-off is yours. Who signs at each level is in
[deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd).
